elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative language states that Customer “shall not pay Vendor any liquidated damages” and expressly includes the former fifteen-percent weekly amount within that prohibition.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative language states that Customer “shall not pay Vendor any ... penalty.” The rendered clause contains no affirmative penalty obligation.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer must be an early-termination fee triggered by early termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not establish an early-termination fee or an early-termination trigger.

elements.element: The early-termination fee must be capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No three-month cap appears in the operative language; it appears only in the non-operative margin comment.

elements.element: The early-termination fee must be the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative language does not designate an early-termination fee as the sole liquidated amount. The only such statement is in the non-operative margin comment.

result.reason: The redline minimally converts the late-payment liquidated-damages obligation into an express prohibition and therefore reaches the preferred position in the clause presented. It leaves the invoice due date and Vendor's other remedies untouched. The fallback is not independently implemented because its trigger, cap, and exclusivity terms appear only in the non-operative margin comment.
